Before daybreak, Nacho is already awake. He has to sweep away the dust that drifts onto the windows from the shore, tidy up the tools Grandma left strewn across the floor yesterday, mend the holes large and small in the fin net, and then carry the pot of rainwater from outside the door to the stove. Only after all of this is done does he sit down by the window and quietly gaze at his fin tank.
At the city inside the tank.
A model of an Aegirian city, which he had placed in the tank only a few days ago. Beside the tank lie a dozen or so old models he had taken out before. Making these models had long since become a habit of Nacho's.
Why?
Perhaps because Grandma always said they did not belong here. He didn't know where he was supposed to belong, but he tried very hard to imagine it.
He would point to his newest model and tell Grandma about the underwater life he imagined. Spherical living pods that could be combined freely, or floating districts all linked together by pipes...
Of course, back then he could not have known that Grandma had long forgotten what an Aegirian city looked like. She wearily went along with what he said, unable to bring herself to interrupt him.
And so the models on the windowsill piled up. Which one of them did an Aegirian city actually resemble? He didn't know, but he was already trying very hard to imagine it, to imagine what a place to belong ought to look like.
Clementia looked at the rows of city models on the windowsill and made no attempt to hide her surprise.
"Such a talent for design... with a little training, you really could work in urban design."
"Supervisor Clementia, me?"
"Of course, Nacho. If you don't wish to go to Aegir, you can finish all of the design work right here, and then one day watch the city you designed with your own hands rise above the distant sea."
"I'm really happy, thank you, but... I'm not sure I'm still seriously designing these buildings anymore..."
Nacho stared at the model in the fin tank. Tiny fins swam through its gaps in twos and threes.
"These hollow structures... I can't say anymore what I imagined, or why I designed them that way, like I used to. I guess it's just so the fins in the tank can swim through them. The tank is where they live, after all. If I put my model in there and it's no use to them at all, that would be too unkind."
"So, what is your decision?"
"I think I'll pass. These models... let's just say they aren't Aegirian cities, only places for these fins to call home. Look... there are fin eggs stuck to it."
